title: umbraflow-project.json
$comment: The one shape authority for umbraflow-project.json. The offline project kit and the runtime loader both compile these exact bytes out of the framework schema catalog, so no reader can accept a document another refuses; a second, narrower reader in either of them would be the weaker of two spellings and would decide. A deployment block IS its registration, stated as intent: it names files, and the loader derives every digest from the bytes it read. No member the loader reads is a hash and no project author types one there. template_cuts is the single deliberate exception and states why in its own $comment: its sources are not files of this project, so a content address is the only name they have. Every path member is typed as a bare non-empty string and given its spelling rule by requireManifestSpelling in modules/deployment/source/deployment/project-directory.cpp, because that rule is task_platform::ConfinedRoot's own (confined-file.hpp:52-55). Stating it a second time as a regular expression would be two spellings of one thing.

runtime_artifact.$comment: A directory, not a file: the installer reads runtime-model.toml and runtime-artifact.manifest.json out of a root by those fixed names.

policy_artifact.$comment: Optional exact PolicyArtifact bytes. When absent, production uses the Operator-owned deny-all artifact; the project never evaluates policy.

template_cuts.$comment: The Locator templates `project build` cuts for this project, and the one place a project author writes a hash. A cut names its sources by sha256 and by nothing else, because a source is a capture of a running target rather than a file of this project: it is not in the source tree, it is not in the release, and a path member would name a screenshot on whichever machine happened to take it. That is the whole point of the capability -- no repository need reference a screenshot path -- so the alternative is not a nicer spelling, it is the defect. The member is stated even when it is empty, on the same terms as resources, so that a project that cuts nothing says so rather than being read as one whose declaration went missing. Resolving a hash to bytes is deliberately not the kit's job and never becomes it: the corpus root arrives at `project build --frames-root PATH`, outside this document, which is why nothing here can name a directory. Declared at the root rather than inside a deployment because generated/templates/ is one flat namespace for the whole build -- generatedTemplates in modules/project/source/project/project-kit.cpp refuses a repeated template path across all of them -- and because no member of a cut names a deployment.

Sha256.$comment: A content address, lowercase hex with no prefix, spelled as every other published document under schema/ spells one. ContentHash::parse wants the canonical `sha256:` prefix and the reader adds it; carrying the prefix here would make the member disagree with every other digest a project or the framework writes down.

PixelRect.$comment: A region of a source image in that image's own pixels. The lower bound on width and height is PixelRect::create's own refusal of an empty rect, restated here so the document is refused where it is written rather than where it is used. There is no upper bound but the representable one: the real bound is the source's extent, which only the decoded image knows, and image::cutRgba8Template judges it there.

template.$comment: Where the cut lands under the build's generated/templates/ family. Relative and inside that family; normalizeTemplatePath states both refusals, because leaving the family is a property of the path once resolved rather than of its spelling.

source_sha256s.$comment: Every source the cut is taken from, in the order they compose. The first decides the colour plane and the whole list decides the alpha plane: a pixel is opaque only where every source agrees, so cutting one region from several captures is how a template stops carrying a background that moves. One source is legal and means a fully opaque template.

PluginAuthoring.$comment: Which of the two authoring paths wrote the Luau module `plugin` names. `generated` is the declarative tier: the project kit produced the module from an umbraflow-declarative-workflow-tool/v1 declaration. `hand-written` is the exception: the author wrote the whole five-function module. The author states it because only the author knows it -- nothing in the module's bytes carries it, and a path convention would be a rule the kit knows and the loader cannot apply, which is how the two readers drift apart.

PluginJustification.$comment: Why this deployment writes a whole five-function Luau module instead of a declarative-tools declaration: it must name the umbraflow-declarative-workflow-tool/v1 member or semantic that cannot express the behaviour. Required of a hand-written plugin and refused for a generated one, because demanding a reason from the declarative tier is demanding a false one. PRESENCE ONLY, over ASCII whitespace alone: the pattern refuses a value made of spaces, tabs, newlines, carriage returns, form feeds and vertical tabs, and accepts one made only of U+00A0 or any other non-ASCII space. No reader here judges whether the text is true, and no reader can; a justification that names the wrong member -- or that is a lone NO-BREAK SPACE -- is a review finding at plugin acceptance, not a refusal. See docs/pitfalls/checks-that-cannot-fail.md.

journal_payload_schemas.$comment: The payload schema files this deployment supplies. The journal event schema manifest names each of them by sha256 and never by path, so which file answers for which event type is decided by the bytes rather than by a name written down twice.

effect_payload_schemas.$comment: The effect payload schema files this deployment supplies. No manifest names them: the Tool Catalog's effect_payload_sha256s names each by sha256, which is the only route their bytes have into tool_catalog_hash, and the payload_schema_hash inside an OP:EffectEnvelope is what selects which of them judges it.

observed_instance_identity_schemas.$comment: The identity schema documents this deployment supplies for the observed instances it can publish. Each is a JSON Schema document declaring its own absolute $id, which the compiled authority reads from the bytes rather than restating. The registration's observed_instance_identity_schema_hashes pins each by the sha256 of these exact documents, so the set the deployment supplies and the set the registration owns are one set: a schema bytes moved under a stored session moves project_registration_hash, and a validator for bytes the registration never pinned cannot be added. The member is stated even when it is empty, on the same terms as resources, so a project whose plugin observes nothing says so rather than being read as one whose declaration went missing.

if.$comment: The direct-plugin tier's admission gate, stated where both readers reach it. The guard restates required so this decision does not depend on which keyword the evaluator visits first.

else.$comment: A generated adapter IS the declarative tier and has nothing to justify. The member is refused rather than ignored: a gate that accepted one here would be asking the declarative tier to invent a reason, which is the thing the justification exists to prevent.
